subject: MSA / Order Form: inspection rights timing and artifact handback
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechinc.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medtechinc.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form: inspection scope and evidence handback

Hi Olga,

Thanks for sending the latest order form. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and the attached security exhibit and surfaced a handful of concerns we need to align on before we can sign:

- Inspection boundaries: the draft gives broad "inspection rights" language that could allow access to production environments. For compliance reasons we need this limited to non-production or to "sampled" artifacts. Can Redwood confirm a non-prod gating approach?
- Evidence cadence: we prefer a runbook that lets us accept SOC 2 report bundles and periodic artifact snapshots rather than ad-hoc requests. Is there a formal handback schedule you can commit to (e.g., quarterly report + 10-day artifact transfer window)?
- Pen test timing and notice: MedTech requires 30-60 days notice for third-party pen tests that interface with our environment and would like a short on-call window during tests. We also need a list of approved testing vendors.

I attached a redline (MSA_redline_v3.pdf) with inline suggestions. If Redwood can accept a scoped inspection approach and an evidence handback calendar, we can move forward fast.

Can you loop in the technical contact who will own staging access and logs? I copied MedTech legal so they can comment on specifics.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Legal — MedTech Inc

Attachment: MSA_redline_v3.pdf (redlined MSA, 6 pages)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechinc.com>
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form: inspection scope and evidence handback

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I read the attachments and discussed with product and legal. High-level proposal below to keep the commercial flow moving while addressing MedTech needs: 

1) Scoped inspection: Redwood agrees to limit live "inspection" to non-production environments by default. For sampling on prod data we propose a mutually agreed sampling plan (e.g., sampled tenant snapshots, PII redaction rules, or a production data extract under strict controls).

2) Evidence cadence: we can commit to a quarterly evidence handback: quarterly SOC 2 bundle (when available) + a 10-business-day artifact delivery window for requested ticketed artifacts (logs, config snapshots, CBOR manifests). We will document the runbook and a single point of contact for ticket triage.

3) Pen test coordination: Redwood will provide a 45-day notice window as a standard (flexible between 30–60 days by mutual agreement), plus a 72-hour on-call window for escalations during the test. We will provide the list of preferred vendors and accept vendor-specific NDAs.

We can capture this in the Order Form appendix (S7) so the MSA stays clean. I've attached a short OrderForm_S7_redlines.docx with the proposed appendix language and a sample runbook. Can Connor and Karthik confirm the staging access model and the ephemeral creds approach?

If that sounds acceptable I can circulate a clean MSA + Order Form appendix for signature and a DocuSign link.

—Olga
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_S7_redlines.docx (proposed appendix and runbook)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medtechinc.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form: inspection scope and evidence handback

Laura / Olga — quick technical notes from infra/ops to make sure the appendix maps to implementation:

- Non-prod gating: we propose a dedicated staging environment that mirrors production controls but contains synthetic or redacted data for inspection. For any exception where sampled production artifacts are required we will use a scoped snapshot process: snapshot taken by Redwood, PII hashed, access via secure transfer, and retention limited to the agreed 10-day window.
- Ephemeral access: we use short-lived credentials (max 8 hours) scoped to specific artifact queries. All actions will be audited; log bundles (immutable) are deliverable as part of the artifact package.
- Pen test vendor integration: we maintain a list of third-party vendors we have previously onboarded; new vendors will require a brief technical intake (2–3 business days). We can support a 48–72 hour responder on the ops side during the agreed test window.

I reviewed Olga's appendix and it includes these controls; small ask: can MedTech confirm which log retention window you need for forensic review (30 / 90 / 180 days)? That determines how we package the artifact set.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Staff SRE — Redwood Inference

Hi Olga / Connor — thank you, this is helpful and close to what we need. A few closing asks before we finalize: 

- Please include the vendor pre-approval list in the appendix (John Mercer from our audit desk is copied and will confirm).
- Confirm log retention option: we will request 90-day retention for security logs used in forensic review. If there are platform constraints, propose a compensating control.
- Add a clause for a 48-hour ops responder during active pen test windows (we prefer 48 but can accept 72 if needed).

If Redwood can incorporate the three bullet points above into the S7 appendix and provide a DocuSign-ready Order Form, Legal will sign and we can schedule the onboarding call in the next two weeks.
